First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{csc}⁡x(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-{sin}^{3}⁡x)=3\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-3\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot {sin}^{3}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the identity $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}$ to further simplify the expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-3\operatorname{csc}⁡x\cdot {sin}^{3}⁡x & =3\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-3\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot {sin}^{3}⁡x \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}-\frac{3{sin}^{3}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{3\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}-\frac{3{sin}^{2}⁡x\cdot \cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}} \\  & =3-3{sin}^{2}⁡x \\  & =3(1-{sin}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the identity ${cos}^{2}⁡x=1-{sin}^{2}⁡x$  to rewrite the expression on the right-hand side.

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
3\operatorname{csc}⁡x(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-{sin}^{3}⁡x)=3{cos}^{2}⁡x
$$
